gaps.title: Missing automatic access control based on Moodle departments and courses
gaps.jtbd: When a user logs in via Moodle SSO, I want the system to automatically restrict their access to closed strains and analytical reports based on their Moodle department and courses, so that access control is synchronized and secure without manual configuration.
gaps.acceptanceCriteria: Given a user logs in via Moodle SSO with a specific department and course, When they attempt to access closed strains or analytical reports, Then the system should allow or deny access based on those Moodle department and courses.
gaps.reason: The brief explicitly requires 'Автоматическое разграничение прав доступа к закрытым штаммам и аналитическим отчетам на основе кафедр и курсов Moodle'. The AuthController saves the department on the User, but there is no mechanism enforcing access control to strains or reports based on this department or courses anywhere in the application.

gaps.title: Missing robust external LMS fallback mechanism
gaps.jtbd: When the external Moodle LMS fails, I want the system to provide an autonomous fallback mechanism, so that users can still access the archive and analytical reports.
gaps.acceptanceCriteria: Given the external Moodle LMS is unreachable, When a user attempts to log in, Then the system should allow them to authenticate via an autonomous fallback mechanism using local credentials.
gaps.reason: The brief explicitly requires 'Устойчивость к сбоям внешней LMS (автономный fallback)'. While there is a generic `/api/v1/auth/login` endpoint and a `fallback_password` field in `SsoLoginRequest`, there is no real resilience or failover logic detecting an LMS failure and switching to a fallback mode, or allowing users originally created via SSO to reset their fallback password or authenticate reliably when SSO is down. A domain-standard fallback for an SSO integration implies a reliable, dedicated offline/local authentication path when the primary provider fails.
